record.paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
record.original_question: Fix natural numbers a1,...,ar. Does there exist a number p, depending only on these degrees, such that for every polynomial ring W over k and every homogeneous ideal J with minimal homogeneous generator degrees a1,...,ar, the projective dimension pd(W/J) is at most p, independently of the number of variables of W?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Fix a positive integer r and natural numbers a_1, a_2, ..., a_r. Does there exist a number p = p(a_1, ..., a_r), depending only on these degrees, such that for every field k, every polynomial ring W = k[x_1, ..., x_N] (in any number N of variables), and every homogeneous ideal J ⊂ W which admits a minimal homogeneous system of generators of degrees a_1, ..., a_r, the projective dimension pd(W/J) of W/J as a W-module satisfies pd(W/J) ≤ p, with the bound p independent of N?
artifact.status_search_result: This is Stillman's conjecture, proved by Ananyan and Hochster in 2016 ("Small Subalgebras of Polynomial Rings and Stillman's Conjecture", arXiv:1610.09268). They established the existence of a uniform upper bound for the projective dimension of any homogeneous ideal generated by forms of prescribed degrees, independent of the number of variables. Subsequent work (e.g., Erman–Sam–Snowden; explicit bounds papers) has refined and reproved the result.

status_evidence.title: Small Subalgebras of Polynomial Rings and Stillman's Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Ananyan and Hochster prove Stillman's conjecture: existence of a uniform bound on projective dimension for ideals generated by forms of given degrees, independent of the number of variables.
status_evidence.claim: Stillman's conjecture was proved by Ananyan and Hochster in 2016.

status_evidence.title: Explicit Stillman bounds for all degrees
status_evidence.snippet: Provides explicit projective-dimension bounds in the setting of Stillman's conjecture for all degrees.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up work gives explicit Stillman bounds, confirming the conjecture is settled.
